## Statement

## Statement

Let $X$ be a finite nonempty set, let $(p_x)$ be a probability vector, let $\rho_x$ be density operators on a nonzero finite-dimensional space $H_B$, and let $\bar\rho:=\sum_xp_x\rho_x$. For a finite POVM $(E_y)_{y\in Y}$ on $H_B$, define $w(y\mid x):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho_xE_y)$, $q_y:=\sum_xp_xw(y\mid x)$, and the classical mutual information

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

Then

$$I(X:Y)\le\chi(\{p_x,\rho_x\})=S(\bar\rho)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$

## Statement

Consider a finite DMN as in [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]]. Let $\mathcal S$ be a source-node set, let $\mathcal D$ be a destination-node set, and let each source $k\in\mathcal S$ send an independent message of rate $R_k$ to every destination. For a finite time-sharing variable $Q$, choose
$$P_Q\prod_{k=1}^N P_{X_k|Q}\prod_{k=1}^N P_{\hat Y_k|Y_k,X_k,Q}.$$
For every destination $d\in\mathcal D$ and every nonempty cut set $A\subseteq[N]$ with $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ and $d\notin A$, the noisy-network-coding inner bound is
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}R_k < I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c}\mid X_{A^c},Q)-I(Y_A;\hat Y_A\mid X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c},Q).$$
The closure of the union of these rate tuples, together with the all-zero rate tuple, is achievable; the separate zero tuple is attained by singleton message sets even if some cut expression is negative. A constant reconstruction $\hat Y_k$ is permitted at any node.
exact_consumer_facts: [F1] [[thm-finite-multisource-multicast-noisy-network-coding-inner-bound]]: for the one-source, one-destination three-node network, its cut $A=\{s\}$ gives the first mutual-information term, and cut $A=\{s,r\}$ gives the second term.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 Substitute $A=\{s\}$ and $A=\{s,r\}$ into [F1]. The first cut has no source-side reconstruction penalty because the source reconstruction can be constant; the second cut has only the relay penalty $I(Y_r;\hat Y_r|X,X_r,Y)$. 2.1 Subtract the first NNC term from the second and use [F3]: $$I(X,X_r;Y)-I(Y_r;\hat Y_r|X,X_r,Y)-I(X;Y,\hat Y_r|X_r)=I(X_r;Y)-I(Y_r;\hat Y_r|X_r,Y).$$ Thus the stated compress-forward condition makes the second term at least the first. ## Definition

Fix a finite DMC and cost model from [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]], with feasible budget $\Gamma$. A length-$n$, $M$-message code from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code]] is **average-cost feasible** if
$$\frac1{nM}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{t=1}^n c(x_t(m))\le\Gamma.$$
A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable under budget $\Gamma$** if there is a sequence of such codes, for all sufficiently large $n$, whose average errors from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code-errors]] tend to zero and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n\ge R$. The **operational cost-constrained capacity** $C(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of these rates.

For an input probability vector $P_X$, define its expected cost $\bar c(P_X)$ as in [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]]. The **cost-constrained information capacity** is
$$C_I(\Gamma):=\sup_{P_X:\,\bar c(P_X)\le\Gamma} I(P_X;W),$$
where $I(P_X;W)$ and the unconstrained DMC information capacity use natural-log nats as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-capacity]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]. All rates use natural-log nats ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). This definition uses a supremum; attainment is proved separately.
exact_consumer_facts: [F1] [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]] and [[def-cost-constrained-dmc-code-and-capacity]]: each codeword's per-use average cost is an average of the letter costs and the information-capacity constraint is $\mathbb E c(X)\le\Gamma$.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 Every letter has $c(x)\le c_{\max}\le\Gamma$ by [F1]. Therefore every ordinary code satisfies the block cost constraint, and every input distribution satisfies the one-letter cost constraint. Conversely a cost-feasible code or distribution is still an ordinary one, so the two code classes and feasible input sets coincide. [F1, given, algebra]

## Definition

Take $M_n=\lfloor e^{nR}\rfloor$, $L_n=\lceil e^{nr}\rceil$ and draw $M_nL_n$ independent words $X^n(m,l)$ with law $p^{\otimes n}$. For message $m$, the encoder inputs the mixed state $$\rho_{m,n}=\frac1{L_n}\sum_{l=1}^{L_n}\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\rho_{X_i(m,l)}.$$ This is a legitimate finite private randomization of the operational input state; the realized codebook is public. Specifically, $$\mathbb E[1-\operatorname{tr}(\Gamma_{m,l}\beta_{X^n(m,l)})]\le\varepsilon_n+2\sqrt{\varepsilon_n},$$ where $\varepsilon_n\le Ce^{-cn}$ bounds both averaged projector failures. $$|\mathcal U'|\le|\mathcal X|+1,\qquad \mathbb E[d(X,g'(Y,U'))]=\mathbb E[d(X,g(Y,U))],\qquad I(X;U'|Y)\le I(X;U|Y).$$

Let an independent finite $Q$ select branch 1 with probability $\lambda$, set $U=(Q,U_Q)$, and use $g(Y,U)=g_Q(Y,U_Q)$. Then $U-X-Y$, the distortion $\lambda d_1+(1-\lambda)d_2$ is at most $\lambda D_1+(1-\lambda)D_2$, and the finite conditional chain rule gives $I(X;U|Y)=I(X;Q|Y)+I(X;U_Q|Y,Q)=\lambda R_{\rm WZ}(D_1)+(1-\lambda)R_{\rm WZ}(D_2)$ because $Q$ is independent of $(X,Y)$. Applying [F2] to reduce $U$ if necessary proves convexity. [F1, F2, F3, choose, construct]

2.1 On the interior of $[D_{\min},D_{\max}]$, write $s(a,b)=(R_{\rm WZ}(b)-R_{\rm WZ}(a))/(b-a)$. Convexity implies $s(a,b)\le s(b,c)$ whenever $a<b<c$, by writing $b$ as a convex combination of $a,c$. For $D_-<z<D$, this gives $s(D_-,z)\le s(z,D)$, hence $R_{\rm WZ}(z)\le\frac{D-z}{D-D_-}R_{\rm WZ}(D_-)+\frac{z-D_-}{D-D_-}R_{\rm WZ}(D)$; the right side tends to $R_{\rm WZ}(D)$ as $z\uparrow D$, while monotonicity gives $R_{\rm WZ}(z)\ge R_{\rm WZ}(D)$. Each $K_j$ is closed because distortion and mutual information are continuous finite entropy functions by [F3]–[F4]. If every $K_j$ were nonempty, they would be nested closed subsets of this compact space with the finite intersection property: if their total intersection were empty, their open complements would cover the compact space and a finite subcover would force one $K_j$ empty. Thus their intersection is nonempty, yielding a channel feasible at $D_{\min}$ with objective at most $r$, contrary to $r<R_{\rm WZ}(D_{\min})$. It follows that $R_{\rm WZ}(D)>r$ on some right neighborhood of $D_{\min}$; since $R_{\rm WZ}(D)\le R_{\rm WZ}(D_{\min})$ by monotonicity, right continuity follows. ## Statement

Let $x\mapsto\rho_x$ be a finite-input, finite-output memoryless cq channel as in [[def-it-classical-quantum-memoryless-channel]]. With the average-error code convention of [[def-it-cq-channel-block-code-and-error]], its classical capacity in nats per use is
$$C_{\rm cq}=\max_{p\in\Delta(\mathcal X)}\chi_p,\qquad \chi_p:=S\!\left(\sum_xp_x\rho_x\right)-\sum_{x:p_x>0}p_xS(\rho_x).$$
For every $0\le R<C_{\rm cq}$ a sequence of codes with rate tending to $R$ has average error tending to zero, and every reliable sequence has limiting upper rate at most $C_{\rm cq}$. This theorem concerns a fixed finite classical input alphabet and does not assert a single-letter formula for general quantum-input channels.

The Weyl matrices in the fixed ordered basis are $U_{ab}|j\rangle=e^{2\pi i bj/D}|j+a\pmod D\rangle$. Reorder the shared state as $R\otimes\mathbb C^D$ using [F5]. Applying [F9] with retained factor $R$ and twirled factor the sender's $D$-dimensional register gives $I_R/D\otimes I_D/D$, since the retained marginal is $I_R/D$. Reordering back gives $I_D/D\otimes I_R/D$. The supplied finite root-of-unity calculation establishes the phase cancellation for every $D\ge1$. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F5, F9, given, algebra, construct]

## Statement

Let $X,Y,Z$ have a joint pmf on finite alphabets and suppose that, for every $y$ with $p_Y(y)>0$,

$$p_{XZ|y}(x,z)=p_{X|y}(x)p_{Z|y}(z).$$

This is the finite Markov condition $X\to Y\to Z$. Then

$$I(X;Z)\le I(X;Y),$$

with equality if and only if $I(X;Y|Z)=0$, equivalently $X$ and $Y$ are conditionally independent given every positive-mass value of $Z$.

## Definition

Fix a finite DMC and cost model from [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]], with feasible budget $\Gamma$. A length-$n$, $M$-message code from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code]] is **average-cost feasible** if
$$\frac1{nM}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{t=1}^n c(x_t(m))\le\Gamma.$$
A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable under budget $\Gamma$** if there is a sequence of such codes, for all sufficiently large $n$, whose average errors from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code-errors]] tend to zero and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n\ge R$. The **operational cost-constrained capacity** $C(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of these rates.

For an input probability vector $P_X$, define its expected cost $\bar c(P_X)$ as in [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]]. The **cost-constrained information capacity** is
$$C_I(\Gamma):=\sup_{P_X:\,\bar c(P_X)\le\Gamma} I(P_X;W),$$
where $I(P_X;W)$ and the unconstrained DMC information capacity use natural-log nats as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-capacity]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]. All rates use natural-log nats ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). This definition uses a supremum; attainment is proved separately.

exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 If $M=1$, the rate is zero and the converse is immediate. Suppose $M\ge2$. ## Definition

Given an input law $P_X$, let $Q_{P_X}=P_XW$ be its output law. The **information density** is
$$\imath_{P_X}(x;y):=\ln\frac{W(y\mid x)}{Q_{P_X}(y)}$$
when $P_X(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, and is $-\infty$ otherwise. For block sequences define $\imath_{P_X}(x^n;y^n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\imath_{P_X}(x_i;y_i)$, with any sum containing $-\infty$ equal to $-\infty$. On the support of the induced joint law, both numerator and denominator are positive, and the value is finite.
exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-density]]: the information density is $\ln(W(y\mid x)/Q_{P_X^*}(y))$ on the induced joint support, with its block value the coordinate sum.
exact_consumer_steps: 2.1 Draw $M_n$ codewords independently from $P_X^{*\,n}$. Decode to the unique codeword with information density greater than $\ln M_n+n\delta$, using a fixed default output if there is not exactly one. Conditional on the transmitted message, an error is contained in the union of the true-codeword miss event from step 1.1 and the event that some independent competing word passes the threshold. For one competitor $X'^n\sim P_X^{*\,n}$ independent of $Y^n\sim Q_{P_X^*}^{\,n}$, [F2] gives $\mathbb E e^{\imath_{P_X^*}(X'^n;Y^n)}=\sum_{x^n}P_X^{*\,n}(x^n)\sum_{y^n:Q_{P_X^*}^{\,n}(y^n)>0}W^n(y^n\mid x^n)=1$ by [F4], since every output reachable from a positive-probability input has positive $Q_{P_X^*}$ mass. On a false pass, the nonnegative variable $Z=e^{\imath_{P_X^*}(X'^n;Y^n)}$ exceeds $e^{\ln M_n+n\delta}$, so $1=\mathbb E Z\ge e^{\ln M_n+n\delta}\Pr[Z>e^{\ln M_n+n\delta}]$, and the false-pass probability is at most $e^{-\ln M_n-n\delta}$. A union bound over at most $M_n-1$ competitors makes this term at most $e^{-n\delta}$. [F2, F4, step 1.1, algebra]

## Definition

Fix a finite DMC and cost model from [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]], with feasible budget $\Gamma$. A length-$n$, $M$-message code from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code]] is **average-cost feasible** if
$$\frac1{nM}\sum_{m=1}^M\sum_{t=1}^n c(x_t(m))\le\Gamma.$$
A rate $R\ge0$ is **average-error achievable under budget $\Gamma$** if there is a sequence of such codes, for all sufficiently large $n$, whose average errors from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code-errors]] tend to zero and satisfy $\liminf_{n\to\infty}n^{-1}\ln M_n\ge R$. The **operational cost-constrained capacity** $C(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of these rates.

For an input probability vector $P_X$, define its expected cost $\bar c(P_X)$ as in [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]]. The **cost-constrained information capacity** is
$$C_I(\Gamma):=\sup_{P_X:\,\bar c(P_X)\le\Gamma} I(P_X;W),$$
where $I(P_X;W)$ and the unconstrained DMC information capacity use natural-log nats as in [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-capacity]] and [[def-natural-logarithm]]. All rates use natural-log nats ([[def-natural-logarithm]]). This definition uses a supremum; attainment is proved separately.

## Definition

Let $W(y\mid x)$ be the finite DMC [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel]] and $c:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ the finite input cost from [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]], with feasible budget $\Gamma$ from [[def-cost-constrained-dmc-code-and-capacity]]. A deterministic length-$n$ feedback code with $M\ge1$ equiprobable messages consists of causal maps
$$f_t:[M]\times\mathcal Y^{t-1}\to\mathcal X\quad(1\le t\le n)$$
and a decoder $g:\mathcal Y^n\to[M]$. Given message $m$, its channel law is the product of the row probabilities $W(y_t\mid f_t(m,y^{t-1}))$. Its expected average cost is
$$\frac1n\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E[c(X_t)],$$
where the expectation is over the uniform message and channel outputs. It is feasible when this quantity is at most $\Gamma$; its average error is $\Pr[g(Y^n)\ne M]$ and its rate is $n^{-1}\ln M$ nats per use. The feedback operational capacity $C_{\rm fb}(\Gamma)$ is the supremum of rates for which feasible codes for all sufficiently large blocklengths have average error tending to zero and limiting inferior rate at least the stated rate. The no-feedback subclass consists of encoders $f_t$ that do not depend on $y^{t-1}$; it includes every ordinary fixed-length code from [[def-fixed-length-channel-code]]. Its rate uses the natural logarithm [[def-natural-logarithm]].

exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 For each time $t$ and each positive-probability history $h=y^{t-1}$, the causal encoder and memoryless channel give the finite Markov chain $M\to X_t\to Y_t$. By chain rule [F1] and data processing [F2], $I(M;Y^n)\le\sum_{t=1}^n\mathbb E_{Y^{t-1}}C_I(\mathbb E[c(X_t)\mid Y^{t-1}])$, applying the definition of $C_I$ to each conditional input law, whose cost is at least $c_{\min}$. [A1, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

## Statement

Let $W$ be a finite DMC, $c:\mathcal X\to[0,\infty)$ a finite letter cost, and $\Gamma\ge c_{\min}$. The feasible set $\{P_X:\bar c(P_X)\le\Gamma\}$ is nonempty and compact, and $C_I(\Gamma)$ from [[def-cost-constrained-dmc-code-and-capacity]] is attained with $0\le C_I(\Gamma)\le\ln|\mathcal X|$. The function $\Gamma\mapsto C_I(\Gamma)$ is nondecreasing and concave on $[c_{\min},\infty)$. If $\Gamma>c_{\min}$, then for every maximizing law $P_X^*$ the laws
$$P_{X,\epsilon}:=(1-\epsilon)P_X^*+\epsilon\delta_{x_{\min}},\qquad 0<\epsilon<1,$$
have cost strictly below $\Gamma$ whenever $P_X^*$ has cost $\Gamma$, and $I(P_{X,\epsilon};W)\to C_I(\Gamma)$ as $\epsilon\downarrow0$.
exact_consumer_facts: [F3] [[def-finite-dmc-cost-model]] and [[lem-cost-constrained-dmc-information-capacity-properties]]: $C_I(u)$ is nondecreasing and concave for $u\ge c_{\min}$ and satisfies $0\le C_I(u)\le\ln|\mathcal X|$.

[A1, F1, F2, F3, given, algebra]

2.1 Give a uniform random index $T\in[n]$ independent of the code and set $U=\mathbb E[c(X_T)\mid T,Y^{T-1}]$. Then $U\ge c_{\min}$, $\mathbb E U=n^{-1}\sum_t\mathbb E c(X_t)\le\Gamma$, and $C_I(U)$ is integrable by [F3]. ## Statement

All logarithms, mutual informations and rates in this lemma are in nats. Consider a memoryless network with finite node set $[N]$, source set $\mathcal S$, destination set $\mathcal D$, and independent uniform source messages, each required by every destination. Alphabets are either all finite, as in [[def-finite-discrete-memoryless-network-and-code]], or finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces with constant coordinates allowed. Encoders are measurable functions of a node's own message and its past outputs; a destination knows its own message. Choose a finite variable $Q$ and measurable kernels with joint law
$$P_Q\prod_k P_{X_k|Q}\,W(dy_{[N]}|x_{[N]})\prod_k P_{\hat Y_k|X_k,Y_k,Q}.$$
Assume AC in the Euclidean case. For each positive-probability $q$, require a measurable version of the local log likelihood
$$\iota_{k,q}=\log\frac{dP_{\hat Y_k|X_k,Y_k,q}}{dP_{\hat Y_k|X_k,q}}(\hat Y_k)$$
to exist and be square-integrable under the target law. For a destination $d$, nonempty $A\subseteq[N]\setminus\{d\}$, and $U\subseteq A^c\setminus\{d\}$, put $C_0=(A\cup U)^c$, let $P_{d,q}$ be the target marginal law of $(X_{[N]},\hat Y_{[N]},Y_d)$ given $q$, and define
$$Q_{d,A,U,q}=P_{X_{A^c},\hat Y_{C_0},Y_d|q}\prod_{k\in A}P_{X_k|q}\prod_{k\in A\cup U}P_{\hat Y_k|X_k,q}.$$
Require $P_{d,q}\ll Q_{d,A,U,q}$ with a measurable square-integrable log likelihood under $P_{d,q}$. Require all mutual informations in the following cut expression to be finite:
$$F_d(A)=I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c}|X_{A^c},Q)-I(Y_A;\hat Y_A|X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c},Q).$$
These likelihood and finiteness hypotheses hold automatically for finite alphabets; zero-mass target atoms are omitted. At any chosen constrained node let $c_k\ge0$ be a measurable input cost. Require either $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)^2]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)]<\Gamma_k$, or a deterministic input whose cost is at most $\Gamma_k$. The latter case includes an identically zero input under a zero budget. Unconstrained nodes and constant coordinates are permitted.

Every nonnegative rate tuple satisfying
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}r_k<F_d(A)$$
for every $d\in\mathcal D$ and nonempty $A$ with $d\notin A$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ is achievable by deterministic measurable causal codes. Each constrained node can satisfy $\sum_{t=1}^m c_k(X_{k,t})\le m\Gamma_k$ on every realized transmitted input sequence of code length $m$, and hence also its expected average-cost constraint. The closure of the union of these regions over admissible laws is achievable. Constant reconstructions are permitted. The separate all-zero tuple is achievable whenever one can choose fixed inputs obeying any imposed costs, regardless of negative cut expressions.
exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[lem-finite-or-euclidean-likelihood-ratio-network-coding]]: for finite alphabets the square-integrable local and packing likelihood hypotheses give precisely the displayed cut inner region, with finite coded time sharing, constant reconstructions, closure, and a separate singleton-message zero tuple; its finite assertion uses no choice axiom.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 For each positive-probability value of $Q$, use the target law in the statement. Its alphabets are finite. A target-positive joint atom has positive local marginal-reconstruction probability and positive reference probability for every reference law in [F2], because all its displayed marginal factors are positive. Thus every required likelihood ratio is finite on target support; the finitely many log values are bounded and hence square-integrable. All cut informations are finite. No cost constraint is imposed. 2.1 Apply [F2] with this law and source/destination sets. Its independent messages, causal encoders and destination side information have exactly the conventions of [F1]. Its cut expression is $I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c}|X_{A^c},Q)-I(Y_A;\hat Y_A|X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c},Q)$ for every required $A,d$, so every tuple satisfying the displayed strict inequalities is achievable. A constant reconstruction is allowed in [F2] and contributes zero local and conditional information. [F1, F2, step 1.1, given]

3.1 The closure-of-union conclusion follows from [F2], or by choosing a sequence of strict-region laws and rate tuples tending to the claimed point and selecting successively longer codes with error tending to zero and rates tending to that point. ## Statement

Let $Q,X,Z,Y$ be finite random variables and suppose the channel law $P_{Y|X,Z,Q}$ depends on $Q$ only through $(X,Z)$; equivalently, $Q-(X,Z)-Y$ is a Markov chain. Then
$$I(X;Y\mid Z)\ge I(X;Y\mid Z,Q).$$
Thus, for a fixed finite channel and fixed side information $Z$, averaging input laws over a time-sharing variable cannot increase the average conditional mutual information.
exact_consumer_facts: [F5] [[lem-finite-conditional-channel-mutual-information-concave-input-law]]: for a fixed channel $W(y|x,z)$, averaging over an input time-sharing variable $Q$ gives $I(X;Y|Z)\ge I(X;Y|Z,Q)$.
exact_consumer_steps: 2.1 Since conditional mutual information is nonnegative, each summand is at most $I(M,Y_r^{i-1};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})$. Given $(M,Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$, the current inputs are fixed by causality in either model, and [F1] makes the current output depend on those variables only through $(X_i,X_{r,i})$. Thus the summand equals $I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})$. For the fixed channel $W_Y$, the past $Y^{i-1}$ is a time-sharing variable independent of the current output once the current inputs are fixed. Applying [F5] gives $I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i\mid Y^{i-1})\le I(X_i,X_{r,i};Y_i)$. [F1, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 For the second cut, $I(M;Y^n)\le I(M;Y^n,Y_r^n)=\sum_i I(M;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1})$. The relay input $X_{r,i}$ is determined by the past. Given the past and $M$, the source input is determined; memorylessness therefore reduces each term to $I(X_i;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid Y^{i-1},Y_r^{i-1},X_{r,i})$. Conditional on a fixed $X_{r,i}=x_r$, the past is a time-sharing variable for the fixed channel $W_{(Y,Y_r)|X,x_r}$. Applying [F5] and averaging over $X_{r,i}$ bounds the term by $I(X_i;Y_i,Y_{r,i}\mid X_{r,i})$. [F1, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

## Statement

$$I(X_1^n;Y_1^n|X_2^n)\le I(X_1^n;Y_2^n|X_2^n),\qquad I(X_2^n;Y_2^n|X_1^n)\le I(X_2^n;Y_1^n|X_1^n).$$

$$I(X:Y):=\sum_{x,y:p_xw(y\mid x)>0}p_xw(y\mid x)\ln\frac{w(y\mid x)}{q_y}.$$

## Statement

Let $X$ take values in an alphabet $\mathcal X$ of size $m\ge2$, let $Y$ be finite, and let $\widehat X$ be an estimator in the same alphabet generated from $Y$, so the joint pmf factors as $p_{XY\widehat X}=p_{XY}p_{\widehat X|Y}$. Put $P_e=\mathbb P[\widehat X\ne X]$ and define

$$h_2(t):=-t\ln t-(1-t)\ln(1-t),\qquad 0\ln0:=0.$$

Then

$$H(X|Y)\le h_2(P_e)+P_e\ln(m-1)\le \ln2+P_e\ln m.$$

For $m=1$, $X$ is constant and $H(X|Y)=0$.

## Statement

Let $H_A,H_B,H_C$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner-product spaces and let $\rho_{ABC}$ be a density operator on their ordered tensor product. Write $\rho_{AB},\rho_{BC},\rho_B$ for its marginals using the partial traces in [[def-qc-partial-trace]]. Then
$$S(\rho_{AB})+S(\rho_{BC})\ge S(\rho_B)+S(\rho_{ABC}),$$
where $S(\rho)=-\operatorname{tr}(\rho\ln\rho)$ with $0\ln0:=0$ as in [[def-it-von-neumann-entropy]].
exact_consumer_facts: [F6] [[thm-it-finite-strong-subadditivity]]: for every finite tripartite state, $S(AB)+S(BC)\ge S(B)+S(ABC)$.
exact_consumer_steps: 2.2 Let $p_i(x)=M^{-1}|\{m:x_i(m)=x\}|$ and $\bar\omega=M^{-1}\sum_m\omega_m$. By [F17], its $i$th marginal is $\bar\rho_i=\sum_xp_i(x)\rho_x$, which is a state by [F16]. For any bipartite state $\tau_{AC}$, tensor it with the unique state on a one-dimensional middle register $B=\mathbb C$: the four entropies in [F6] become $S(\tau_A),S(\tau_C),0,S(\tau_{AC})$, because tensoring with this factor leaves the spectrum unchanged. Thus [F6] implies $S(\tau_{AC})\le S(\tau_A)+S(\tau_C)$; iterating gives $S(\bar\omega)\le\sum_iS(\bar\rho_i)$. Product entropy is additive: diagonalize each $\rho_{x_i(m)}$ by [F12], so every positive product eigenvalue has logarithm equal to the sum of its coordinate logarithms by [F13]; zero eigenvalues contribute zero by [F2]. Summing these finite terms gives $S(\omega_m)=\sum_iS(\rho_{x_i(m)})$. ## Definition

For an input probability vector $P_X$ on $\mathcal X$ ([[def-finite-probability-vector]]), let $P_{XY}(x,y):=P_X(x)W(y\mid x)$ and $Q_{P_X}(y):=\sum_xP_X(x)W(y\mid x)$. Write $I(P_X;W):=I(X;Y)$ for this joint law, using [[def-it-finite-mutual-information]]. The **single-letter information capacity** is
$$C(W):=\sup_{P_X} I(P_X;W),$$
measured in nats per channel use. The finite-dimensional maximum is attained, as proved in [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]].
exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[lem-discrete-memoryless-channel-capacity-is-attained]] and [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-capacity]]: $C(W)=\max_PI(P,W)$ is finite and attained; the CAID set $\Pi(W)$ is nonempty.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 Choose any CAID and let $Q^*$ be its output law. By [F3], every row is supported on $Q^*$ and has divergence $d_x:=D(W_x\|Q^*)\le C(W)$. For every CAID $P$, [F5] gives $\mathbb E[\imath_P(X;Y)\mid X=x]=C(W)$ on each positive-mass input and $\operatorname{Var}(\imath_P(X;Y))=V(P,W)$. [F2, F3, F5, given]

1.2 The set $\Pi(W)$ is compact by finite-simplex compactness and continuity of $I(P,W)$, and [F4] supplies a minimum-dispersion CAID. Since $Q^*$ is positive on every globally reachable output, there is a neighborhood $U$ of $\Pi(W)$ in which every $(PW)(y)$ on that support is bounded below by a positive constant. On $U$, the finite formulas for $V(P,W)$ and $T(P,W):=\sum_xP(x)\mathbb E_{W_x}|\imath_P(x;Y)-D(W_x\|PW)|^3$ are smooth functions of $P$ with bounded derivatives. Shrinking $U$ if needed gives constants $v_0,L,T_0>0$ such that $V(P,W)\ge v_0$, $|\sqrt{V(P,W)}-\sqrt{V(P',W)}|\le L\|P-P'\|_2$ on $U$, and $T(P,W)\le T_0$ there. The derivative bounds follow from [F11] and compactness of the finite-dimensional neighborhood. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F10, F11]

1.3 There is also a global constant $B<\infty$ with $V(P,W)\le B$ for every input law. Indeed, let $w_0$ be the least positive transition probability of $W$. If $P(x)>0$ and $W(y\mid x)>0$, then $(PW)(y)\ge P(x)W(y\mid x)$, so $|\imath_P(x;y)|\le |\ln w_0|+|\ln P(x)|$. The function $t(1+|\ln t|)^2$ extends continuously to zero and is bounded on $[0,1]$; summing the resulting finite bound over $x$ gives $\mathbb E\imath_P^2\le B$ and hence $V(P,W)\le B$. [F1, F2, given, algebra]

## Definition

Given an input law $P_X$, let $Q_{P_X}=P_XW$ be its output law. The **information density** is
$$\imath_{P_X}(x;y):=\ln\frac{W(y\mid x)}{Q_{P_X}(y)}$$
when $P_X(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, and is $-\infty$ otherwise. For block sequences define $\imath_{P_X}(x^n;y^n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\imath_{P_X}(x_i;y_i)$, with any sum containing $-\infty$ equal to $-\infty$. On the support of the induced joint law, both numerator and denominator are positive, and the value is finite.

## Definition

Let $P$ be an input probability vector for the finite DMC $W$, and let $P_Y(y)=\sum_xP(x)W(y\mid x)$. On cells with $P(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, define $\imath_P(x;y)=\ln[W(y\mid x)/P_Y(y)]$; the denominator is then positive. Put
$$V(P,W):=\sum_{x:P(x)>0}P(x)\operatorname{Var}_{W(\cdot\mid x)}[\imath_P(x;Y)].$$
Let $C(W)=\max_P I(P,W)$ and $\Pi(W)=\{P:I(P,W)=C(W)\}$, the nonempty set of capacity-achieving input distributions. Define
$$V_{\min}(W):=\min_{P\in\Pi(W)}V(P,W),\qquad V_{\max}(W):=\max_{P\in\Pi(W)}V(P,W).$$
The local attainment lemma [[lem-it-dmc-dispersion-attains-minimum]] proves these extrema exist. Dispersion is measured in nats squared. In the normal-approximation theorem on this page only the fixed range $0<\epsilon<1/2$ and premise $V_{\min}(W)>0$ are used.
exact_consumer_facts: [F4] [[lem-it-dmc-dispersion-attains-minimum]] and [[def-it-channel-dispersion]]: $V_{\min}(W)$ is attained on $\Pi(W)$ and $V(P,W)$ is the conditional information variance.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.2 The set $\Pi(W)$ is compact by finite-simplex compactness and continuity of $I(P,W)$, and [F4] supplies a minimum-dispersion CAID. Since $Q^*$ is positive on every globally reachable output, there is a neighborhood $U$ of $\Pi(W)$ in which every $(PW)(y)$ on that support is bounded below by a positive constant. On $U$, the finite formulas for $V(P,W)$ and $T(P,W):=\sum_xP(x)\mathbb E_{W_x}|\imath_P(x;Y)-D(W_x\|PW)|^3$ are smooth functions of $P$ with bounded derivatives. Shrinking $U$ if needed gives constants $v_0,L,T_0>0$ such that $V(P,W)\ge v_0$, $|\sqrt{V(P,W)}-\sqrt{V(P',W)}|\le L\|P-P'\|_2$ on $U$, and $T(P,W)\le T_0$ there. The derivative bounds follow from [F11] and compactness of the finite-dimensional neighborhood. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F10, F11]

2.3 Let $P^*\in\Pi(W)$ attain $V_{\min}$. By [F5], under $P^*W$ the information density has mean $C$ and variance $V_{\min}$; its third absolute centered moment $T^*<\infty$. Apply [F8] to $P^{*n}$. For $\gamma=\tfrac12\ln n$, the DT expectation is at most $\Pr\{S_n\le\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma\}+e^{-\gamma},$ by splitting at the displayed threshold. Berry–Esseen [F7] bounds this by $\Phi((t-nC)/\sqrt{nV_{\min}})+1088T^*/(V_{\min}^{3/2}\sqrt n)+n^{-1/2}$, where $t=\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma$. [F4, F5, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Put $a=-z_\epsilon>0$ and $d=\operatorname{dist}_2(P,\Pi(W))$. For $P\in U$, choose a nearest $P_0\in\Pi(W)$, so $V(P_0,W)\ge V_{\min}$. By [F6] and step 1.2, $nI(P,W)-a\sqrt{nV(P,W)}\le nC-a\sqrt{nV_{\min}}-n\alpha d^2+aL\sqrt n\,d\le nC-a\sqrt{nV_{\min}}+\frac{a^2L^2}{4\alpha}.$ Together with step 2.1 this gives the desired $nC+\sqrt{nV_{\min}}z_\epsilon+O(\ln n)$ upper bound for nearby constant-composition codes. [F4, F6, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

## Statement

For every finite DMC, the set $\Pi(W)$ of capacity-achieving input laws is nonempty and compact, and the function $P\mapsto V(P,W)$ is continuous on $\Pi(W)$. Therefore $V_{\min}(W)$ and $V_{\max}(W)$ in [[def-it-channel-dispersion]] are attained.
exact_consumer_facts: [F4] [[lem-it-dmc-dispersion-attains-minimum]] and [[def-it-channel-dispersion]]: $V_{\min}(W)$ is attained on $\Pi(W)$ and $V(P,W)$ is the conditional information variance.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.2 The set $\Pi(W)$ is compact by finite-simplex compactness and continuity of $I(P,W)$, and [F4] supplies a minimum-dispersion CAID. Since $Q^*$ is positive on every globally reachable output, there is a neighborhood $U$ of $\Pi(W)$ in which every $(PW)(y)$ on that support is bounded below by a positive constant. On $U$, the finite formulas for $V(P,W)$ and $T(P,W):=\sum_xP(x)\mathbb E_{W_x}|\imath_P(x;Y)-D(W_x\|PW)|^3$ are smooth functions of $P$ with bounded derivatives. Shrinking $U$ if needed gives constants $v_0,L,T_0>0$ such that $V(P,W)\ge v_0$, $|\sqrt{V(P,W)}-\sqrt{V(P',W)}|\le L\|P-P'\|_2$ on $U$, and $T(P,W)\le T_0$ there. The derivative bounds follow from [F11] and compactness of the finite-dimensional neighborhood. [F1, F2, F3, F4, F10, F11]

2.3 Let $P^*\in\Pi(W)$ attain $V_{\min}$. By [F5], under $P^*W$ the information density has mean $C$ and variance $V_{\min}$; its third absolute centered moment $T^*<\infty$. Apply [F8] to $P^{*n}$. For $\gamma=\tfrac12\ln n$, the DT expectation is at most $\Pr\{S_n\le\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma\}+e^{-\gamma},$ by splitting at the displayed threshold. Berry–Esseen [F7] bounds this by $\Phi((t-nC)/\sqrt{nV_{\min}})+1088T^*/(V_{\min}^{3/2}\sqrt n)+n^{-1/2}$, where $t=\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma$. [F4, F5, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.1 Put $a=-z_\epsilon>0$ and $d=\operatorname{dist}_2(P,\Pi(W))$. For $P\in U$, choose a nearest $P_0\in\Pi(W)$, so $V(P_0,W)\ge V_{\min}$. By [F6] and step 1.2, $nI(P,W)-a\sqrt{nV(P,W)}\le nC-a\sqrt{nV_{\min}}-n\alpha d^2+aL\sqrt n\,d\le nC-a\sqrt{nV_{\min}}+\frac{a^2L^2}{4\alpha}.$ Together with step 2.1 this gives the desired $nC+\sqrt{nV_{\min}}z_\epsilon+O(\ln n)$ upper bound for nearby constant-composition codes. [F4, F6, step 1.2, step 2.1, algebra]

## Statement

Let $W^n$ be the block channel of a finite DMC, let $P_{X^n}$ be any input law, and let $M\ge2$. Define the charged information density $\imath(x^n;y^n)=\ln[W^n(y^n\mid x^n)/(P_{X^n}W^n)(y^n)]$ on the support of $P_{X^n}W^n$. There is a deterministic length-$n$ code with $M$ messages and average error at most
$$\mathbb E\exp\left(-\left[\imath(X^n;Y^n)-\ln\frac{M-1}{2}\right]_+\right),$$
where $(X^n,Y^n)\sim P_{X^n}W^n$. For $M=1$, a zero-error code exists. The conclusion is an average-error bound and does not by itself bound every message's error.
exact_consumer_facts: [F8] [[thm-it-one-shot-decision-threshold-achievability]]: a deterministic code exists with average error at most $\mathbb E e^{-[\imath(X^n;Y^n)-\ln((M-1)/2)]_+}$ for $M\ge2$.
exact_consumer_steps: 2.3 Let $P^*\in\Pi(W)$ attain $V_{\min}$. By [F5], under $P^*W$ the information density has mean $C$ and variance $V_{\min}$; its third absolute centered moment $T^*<\infty$. Apply [F8] to $P^{*n}$. For $\gamma=\tfrac12\ln n$, the DT expectation is at most $\Pr\{S_n\le\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma\}+e^{-\gamma},$ by splitting at the displayed threshold. Berry–Esseen [F7] bounds this by $\Phi((t-nC)/\sqrt{nV_{\min}})+1088T^*/(V_{\min}^{3/2}\sqrt n)+n^{-1/2}$, where $t=\ln((M-1)/2)+\gamma$. [F4, F5, F7, F8, step 1.1, algebra]

3.2 Set $u_n=\epsilon-(1088T^*/V_{\min}^{3/2}+2)n^{-1/2}$ and $t_n=nC+\sqrt{nV_{\min}}\Phi^{-1}(u_n)$, for large $n$ with $u_n>0$. We have $C>0$: if $C=0$, every point-mass input is a CAID and has zero dispersion, contradicting $V_{\min}>0$. Choose $M=1+\lfloor2e^{t_n-\gamma}\rfloor$, which is at least two for large $n$ and satisfies $t\le t_n$ and $\ln M\ge t_n-\gamma-O(1)$. Step 2.3 and [F7] give a deterministic code with average error at most $\epsilon-n^{-1/2}$ and $\ln M\ge nC+\sqrt{nV_{\min}}z_\epsilon-O(\ln n),$ using local Lipschitz continuity of $\Phi^{-1}$ at $\epsilon$ from [F12]. ## Definition

Given an input law $P_X$, let $Q_{P_X}=P_XW$ be its output law. The **information density** is
$$\imath_{P_X}(x;y):=\ln\frac{W(y\mid x)}{Q_{P_X}(y)}$$
when $P_X(x)W(y\mid x)>0$, and is $-\infty$ otherwise. For block sequences define $\imath_{P_X}(x^n;y^n):=\sum_{i=1}^n\imath_{P_X}(x_i;y_i)$, with any sum containing $-\infty$ equal to $-\infty$. On the support of the induced joint law, both numerator and denominator are positive, and the value is finite.
exact_consumer_facts: [F2] [[def-discrete-memoryless-channel-information-density]]: information density is the natural-log likelihood ratio between the channel output law given the input and the output marginal, evaluated on charged support.
exact_consumer_steps: 1.1 Draw codewords $X^n(1),\ldots,X^n(M)$ independently from $P_{X^n}$. Put $Q=P_{X^n}W^n$ and $\tau=\ln((M-1)/2)$. The decoder selects the lowest index $j$ for which $\imath(X^n(j);y^n)>\tau$; if no index passes, it outputs message $1$. This defines a deterministic code decoder for each realized codebook. [F1, F2, F3, given, construct]

2.1 If message $j$ is sent, an error can occur only if its own test fails or an earlier codeword passes. Thus its conditional error is at most $\Pr[\imath(X^n(j);Y^n)\le\tau\mid X^n(j)]+\sum_{k<j}\Pr[\imath(X^n(k);Y^n)>\tau\mid X^n(j)].$ The first probability averaged over the true codeword and output is $\Pr_{P_{X^n}W^n}[\imath\le\tau]$. Each earlier independent codeword and the true output have law $P_{X^n}\otimes Q$, so its averaged term is $\Pr_{P_{X^n}\otimes Q}[\imath>\tau]$. [F1, F2, step 1.1]

3.1 Averaging over the uniform message index gives ensemble-average error at most $\Pr_{P_{X^n}W^n}[\imath\le\tau]+\frac{M-1}{2}\Pr_{P_{X^n}\otimes Q}[\imath>\tau],$ because $M^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^M(j-1)=(M-1)/2$. On the event $\imath>\tau$, the likelihood ratio identity gives $\Pr_{P\otimes Q}[\imath>\tau]=\mathbb E_{PW}[e^{-\imath}\mathbf1_{\{\imath>\tau\}}]$. Therefore this bound equals $\mathbb E_{PW}[e^{-(\imath-\tau)_+}]$. [F2, step 2.1, algebra]

## Statement

For a stationary finite-alphabet source and bounded additive distortion as in [[def-it-stationary-finite-block-information-rdf]], the sequence $R_n(D)$ has a limit for every feasible $D$, and
$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}R_n(D)=\inf_{n\ge1}R_n(D)=R_{\rm block}(D).
$$
The function $R_{\rm block}$ is nonincreasing and convex on $[D_{\min},\infty)$, is zero for $D\ge D_{\rm c}$, and is right-continuous at $D_{\min}$. It is infinite below $D_{\min}$.

If $D<D_{\min}$, choose $\epsilon>0$ with $D+\epsilon<D_{\min}$ and put $g(X)=\min_{\hat x}d(X,\hat x)$. Birkhoff [F6] gives almost-sure convergence of the averages of this bounded function to a finite invariant function $g^*$. For every rational $a$, the limsup orbit set $\limsup_{n\to\infty}T^{-n}\{g^*>a\}$ is strictly invariant and differs from $\{g^*>a\}$ by a null set. Ergodicity makes each such level set have probability zero or one, so $g^*$ is constant almost surely. Dominated convergence and stationarity identify the constant as $\mathbb E g=D_{\min}$. Hence the pointwise-minimum block average converges almost surely to $D_{\min}$, and the probability that any code's distortion exceeds $D+\epsilon$ tends to one. Both operational criteria are therefore infeasible below $D_{\min}$. By [F2], no stationary coupling with mean distortion below $D_{\min}$ exists either, so $R_{\rm erg}(D)=+\infty$; [F3] gives $R_{\rm block}(D)=+\infty$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, given, algebra]

1.3 For every jointly stationary ergodic pair feasible at $D$, the finite-block law is feasible in $R_n(D)$, so $R_n(D)\le n^{-1}I_2(X_0^{n-1};\widehat X_0^{n-1})$. Taking limits and then the infimum over such pairs gives $R_{\rm block}(D)\le R_{\rm erg}(D)$. [F2, F3, given]

2.1 For expected-distortion codes with $\limsup D_n\le D$, eventually $D_n\le D+\epsilon$, giving $R_n(D+\epsilon)\le n^{-1}\log_2M_n$. [F1, F2, F3, step 1.2, given, algebra]

$$Q_{d,A,U,q}=P_{X_{A^c},\hat Y_{C_0},Y_d|q}\prod_{k\in A}P_{X_k|q}\prod_{k\in A\cup U}P_{\hat Y_k|X_k,q}.$$
Require $P_{d,q}\ll Q_{d,A,U,q}$ with a measurable square-integrable log likelihood under $P_{d,q}$. Require all mutual informations in the following cut expression to be finite:
$$F_d(A)=I(X_A;Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c}|X_{A^c},Q)-I(Y_A;\hat Y_A|X_{[N]},Y_d,\hat Y_{A^c},Q).$$
These likelihood and finiteness hypotheses hold automatically for finite alphabets; zero-mass target atoms are omitted. At any chosen constrained node let $c_k\ge0$ be a measurable input cost. Require either $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)^2]<\infty$ and $\mathbb E[c_k(X_k)]<\Gamma_k$, or a deterministic input whose cost is at most $\Gamma_k$. The latter case includes an identically zero input under a zero budget. Unconstrained nodes and constant coordinates are permitted.

Every nonnegative rate tuple satisfying
$$\sum_{k\in A\cap\mathcal S}r_k<F_d(A)$$
for every $d\in\mathcal D$ and nonempty $A$ with $d\notin A$ and $A\cap\mathcal S\ne\varnothing$ is achievable by deterministic measurable causal codes. Each constrained node can satisfy $\sum_{t=1}^m c_k(X_{k,t})\le m\Gamma_k$ on every realized transmitted input sequence of code length $m$, and hence also its expected average-cost constraint. The closure of the union of these regions over admissible laws is achievable. Constant reconstructions are permitted. The separate all-zero tuple is achievable whenever one can choose fixed inputs obeying any imposed costs, regardless of negative cut expressions.

The remaining joint coordinates $(X,Y,\hat Y_{\mathcal Q})$ are an invertible linear image of the independent nonconstant inputs, channel noises and quantization noises: recover inputs first, channel noises from $Y-GX$, and quantization noises from $\hat Y_{\mathcal Q}-Y_{\mathcal Q}$. They therefore have a strictly positive nonsingular Gaussian density. Its needed marginal and conditional densities are likewise Gaussian with positive conditional covariance, so all local and reference likelihood ratios in [F2] exist measurably. Every log ratio is a constant plus a quadratic polynomial in Gaussian variables. [A1, F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

2.1 These log ratios are square-integrable: a quadratic polynomial squared is a finite sum of monomials of degree at most four, and Gaussian fourth moments are finite. Explicitly for a scalar $N(0,v)$ density, integrating by parts twice gives $\mathbb E Z^4=3v^2$; Gaussian coordinates have those scalar marginal laws, and $\mathbb E(Z_i^2Z_j^2)\le(\mathbb E Z_i^4\,\mathbb E Z_j^4)^{1/2}$. The input cost $c_i(x)=x^2$ also has finite second moment $3(P_i')^2$ and mean $P_i'<P_i$.
